resources.string: The tool is off. Turn it on, then add a home.
No home yet. Add one below: Home Assistant, Google Home, SmartThings, a Hue bridge, openHAB, Smart Life or SwitchBot.
%1$s is set up. The keyboard connects when you open the tool.
%1$s stopped accepting the keyboard\'s key. Edit the home and sign in again.
%1$s is not answering. Check the address, or try the remote one.
The keyboard talks only to the homes you list here, each with its own key. Nothing about your home passes through any other service.
Lights, switches, climate, media, scenes and sensors as tiles in the keyboard, live

Every home on the list is connected while the tool runs, and its rooms join the panel\'s tabs. Add a Home Assistant, Google Home, SmartThings, a Hue bridge, an openHAB server, a Smart Life (Tuya) project or a SwitchBot account; more than one is fine.
Tap one to use its address
Falls back to the remote address when the home one does not answer
No browser could open the sign-in page.
Your browser opens Home Assistant\'s own login page. The keyboard gets a key, never your password.
Signed in through the browser. The key renews itself.
Signed in with a long-lived access token.
The sign-in did not match the one started here. Try again.
No server address to sign in to.
In Home Assistant: your profile, Security tab, Long-lived access tokens, Create token. Paste it here; it is kept only on this phone.
Your browser opens Samsung\'s login. SmartThings hands the keyboard a key that renews itself for about a month of disuse.
This build carries no SmartThings sign-in; paste a personal access token instead.
Signed in through the browser. The key renews itself.
Signed in with a personal access token. SmartThings expires these after a day; sign in through the browser for a key that lasts.
From account.smartthings.com/tokens, with the devices, locations and scenes scopes. Valid for 24 hours from creation.
Looking for a Hue bridge on this network… or type its address.
Press the round button on the bridge, then tap Pair within thirty seconds. The bridge gives the keyboard a key of its own.
Paired. The bridge\'s certificate is pinned: a different bridge at this address will be refused.
The bridge\'s button was not pressed. Press it, then tap Pair again.
The API token comes from your openHAB profile (the user menu, Create new API token). Leave it blank if your server lets devices on your network in without one.

Tuya lets other apps in only through a project of your own. At platform.tuya.com, sign up and create a Smart Home cloud project in your app account\'s data centre. Under Devices, Link App Account, scan the QR code with Smart Life or Tuya Smart (Me tab, scan icon). Then copy the project\'s Access ID and Access Secret here. The free plan needs renewing every few months on Tuya\'s site.
The project\'s Overview tab, Authorization Key
Beside the Access ID. Kept only on this phone; it signs each request and is never sent.

In the SwitchBot app: Profile, Preferences, About, then tap App Version ten times. Open the Developer Options that appear and tap Get Token for the token and the secret key. Bluetooth devices need Cloud Services turned on in their settings, and a hub.
Developer Options, Token. SwitchBot allows 10,000 requests a day for it.
Developer Options, Secret Key. Kept only on this phone; it signs each request and is never sent.
Google\'s own screen asks which account and which home, and which kinds of device the keyboard may see. Needs the Google Home app on this phone.
To take the access back on Google\'s side, remove WM Keyboard under your Google account\'s third-party apps, or in the Google Home app\'s linked apps.
Downloading the Google Home part of the keyboard. When it finishes, this screen reopens, and you can choose your home.
The Google Home part did not download. Check the connection, then tap Choose a home again.
The Google Home APIs are not in this build, or Play services is missing on this phone.
Pick the tiles the Favourites tab shows, and hide what you never use
Your rooms as each home orders them; with several homes, the home\'s name comes first. Off, there is Favourites and All.
Locks, alarms, garage doors, gates and sirens take a hold instead of a tap
The command bar at the bottom of the panel sends what you type to Home Assistant\'s Assist, which understands sentences like \"turn off the kitchen lights\". Only Home Assistant has one.
Type a sentence for your home at the bottom of the panel
Which of your assistants answers. The list comes from the server once connected.
Assist answers in the language you are typing in

Home Assistant, a Hue bridge and openHAB hold a connection open so tiles change the moment the house does; SmartThings, Smart Life and SwitchBot are asked every few seconds to once a minute instead. It costs little, but it is a connection.
Connects when you open the tool and drops a minute after you leave it.
Connects when the keyboard comes up, so the panel is live the instant it opens; drops a minute after the keyboard hides.
Keep the last states on the phone
The panel draws your tiles at once from the last session, dimmed until each home confirms them
Let the AI chat control your home
The chat\'s tools include your homes; each one asks before it acts
\"turn off the lights\" in any field offers a chip that sends it to Assist instead of the words
The Favourites tab shows these, in this order. Drag to reorder; the bin takes one off the tab without hiding it.
No favourites yet. Star anything below.
Hidden tiles stay out of every tab and out of search. Tap one to bring it back.
Whole kinds of entity the panel never lists.
Nothing from your homes yet. Open the tool once while connected, or check the connection on the tool\'s page.
Turns things on or off, sets brightness or temperature, runs scenes, on any home on the list. With a Home Assistant, it can also ask Assist in a sentence. Only listed while a home is set up.
The states of your devices and sensors across every home on the list, as they are now
